page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2c.12xlarge is an x86_64 big data server instance operating under the KVM hypervisor. The system incorporates 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 176.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.67 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned.

The defining hardware characteristic of the ecs.d2c.12xlarge is its bundled local storage subsystem, providing 23,837 GB of high-capacity rotational HDD storage. Unlike instances that rely purely on cloud network volumes or low-capacity solid-state drives, this instance bundles an expansive physical HDD footprint directly into the host. The platform contains no hardware graphics acceleration, maintaining a dedicated focus on storage capacity and multi-core computation.

From an operational perspective, pairing high-density mechanical drives with substantial dedicated compute delivers cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing raw capacity and continuous sequential throughput over low-latency random input/output operations. This resource balance fits distributed analytics and storage architectures, including Apache Hadoop clusters, distributed file systems, large-scale extract-transform-load pipelines, and high-volume data ingest nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2c.12xlarge is a dedicated big data instance built on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. It integrates 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, along with 176.0 GB of memory, equating to 3.67 GB per vCPU. The server includes 23,837 GB of bundled local HDD storage and a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps. It features no GPU acceleration. The pairing of substantial multi-core compute capability with an expansive rotational disk array offers high storage capacity density, providing cost-effective data retention and high sequential processing for high-volume ingest pipelines. This configuration is tailored for large-scale data processing frameworks, distributed file systems, batch ETL routines, and big data clusters such as Apache Hadoop.
